description: E2a's Oscillator rack prefab, built from the same primitives its generator uses (SE16/TideModules/build-prefabs.py). Locks the two things V1's acceptance test depends on: that the statically-registered 'Oscillator' primitive is the one in the binary (NOT 'OscillatorNaive', which S8 measured as absent), and that a PITCH jack left unpatched sits at 5 V = 440 Hz. Without the --set-pin the module free-runs at 13.75 Hz, below hearing and indistinguishable from a broken oscillator. Keep this case's script in step with the Oscillator entry in PREFABS in build-prefabs.py. REFERENCE SEEDED ON macOS, 2026-08-18 -- unlike the other two, which came from Linux. CI is Linux, so the first CI run is this reference's first cross-platform comparison; a null-test failure there is more likely to be platform drift than a regression, and E1a's numbers are the yardstick for telling them apart.
tolerance_reason: Measured on Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu 24.04, glibc 2.39) against this case's reference, SynthEditCL V1.6.192, 2026-08-23 (E1c): null -131.1 dBFS, peakdiff -90.3 dBFS = 1 LSB. This case's own residual, measured against its own reference (provenance: seeded on Darwin), replacing gates that were inherited by analogy from E1a's measurement of a DIFFERENT module. The drift-class justification is not merely unmeasured here, it is refuted: E1c showed the core Oscillator at 5 V does not exhibit the phase drift the -67/-62 gates were sized for. Now at the defaults. POSITIVE CONTROL, run before the change: a 3-sample localized glitch injected into the real render is MISSED by the old gates up to 26 LSB (-62 dBFS peak is exactly 26 LSB at 16 bits) and CAUGHT by the defaults from 2 LSB, while the undamaged render still passes. That 26 LSB blind spot is what the old gates cost. NOT VERIFIED: the reverse direction -- a macOS render against a Linux-seeded reference. verify.yml is ubuntu-24.04 only, so nothing runs it on macOS today.
